- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.11 or higher) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.28 or -0.22) — model fails to account for downward pressure.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to premature retracement in forecast.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in the early part of the 30-day horizon.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overreact to recent price highs — suppress early peaks.
- In the final 5–7 days of forecast, model often underestimates upward momentum — especially if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model should reduce forecast slope to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model should adjust downward, but often does not — leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model is sensitive to recent sentiment extremes — if sentiment drops sharply, forecast should not immediately revert to prior trend.
